societies.name: The Cassini Division — Solar Union

scope.continuity: Fall Revolution, Solar Union as depicted in The Cassini Division
scope.period: Established Union before the closing interstellar military intervention
scope.population: Living human and active human-derived Union residents
exclusions: Non-cooperating money enclaves as Union beneficiaries on identical terms
All uploaded Jovian minds as Union citizens

societies.description:
The Solar Union uses nanotechnology to make ordinary material wealth readily available without money. The gathered review explicitly describes a guarantee extending across its citizens, rather than merely a wealthy protagonist with a private fabricator. Guarantees are rated strong within the established commonwealth, while destructive nanotechnology and the reviewer’s doubts about defensive resilience limit any claim of absolute security.

Open elected committees govern both ordinary institutions and the Cassini Division. Combined with common access to decisive productive technology, this supports control toward distributed human ownership, with a broad interval for the difference between formal participation and actual influence. The existence of capable computers does not establish independent AI sovereignty. Useful military, scientific, artistic and care activity continues, so freedom from money and subsistence employment is not treated as universal idleness. Human-derived active residents are a disclosed proxy, while hostile Jovian posthumans and separate money enclaves are not assigned the Union’s rights or institutions.

guarantees.basis: The review explicitly connects nanotechnology to broadly guaranteed material wealth and a moneyless economy.

control.basis: Open elected committees and broadly available productive capacity support distributed human control, with uncertainty about informal influence.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary research, care, creation, administration and maintenance remain work.

societies.name: Lady of Mazes — Teven Coronal’s supported manifolds
societies.society: Shared nanotechnological support beneath culturally distinct manifolds

scope.continuity: Teven Coronal at the beginning of Lady of Mazes
scope.period: Established coronal life before the external dismantling of manifolds
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived coronal residents
exclusions: All perceived people as additional active persons
Every manifold as a separately counted economic order
Later Archipelago arrangements or invasion as unchanged provision

societies.description:
Teven’s residents inhabit distinct culturally curated manifolds while sharing an AI-built habitat and nanotechnological productive support. The gathered accounts describe ordinary goods, services and information as accessible without necessary work or payment. Guarantees are provisionally strong within the functioning coronal, with technology locks and dependence on shared infrastructure limiting any claim of unrestricted individual power. The invasion that dismantles these cultures is a separate condition.

Control remains unresolved. Choosing or inhabiting a narrative environment does not necessarily confer ownership of its physical support, while AI assistance does not by itself prove that humans have no effective authority. The manifolds vary in visible technology and social customs, but this record counts their shared material model once until a concrete allocation difference warrants a split. Living humans and active human-derived residents form an explicit denominator; perception management is not assumed to turn everyone into a stored file. Cultural creation, diplomacy, care and technical work can continue, so nonworking remains null.

societies.name: Ventus — Human society under the Winds’ ceiling
societies.society: Preindustrial humans within a machine-maintained ecosystem

scope.continuity: Ventus, established human settlements before the central mystery is resolved
scope.period: The inherited preindustrial order under the Winds
scope.population: Living human descendants of the colonists
exclusions: The intended automated colony as fully implemented human access
The Winds’ ecosystem protection as a universal individual food floor
Later reconciliation as an already verified new economy

societies.description:
The Winds maintain a terraformed biosphere that would otherwise become poisonous, yet reject advanced human technology as an ecological threat. Human descendants therefore remain in preindustrial monarchies and aristocracies despite the surrounding nanotechnological capacity. This is an interpretive zero variant: machine restrictions retain ordinary human subsistence and craft labor. Ecological misrecognition, rather than a policy to preserve paid jobs, is the relevant cause.

Ultimate control over the technological ceiling lies with the autonomous Winds, near the machine-control end of the axis. Human local rulers retain power within that ceiling but cannot freely deploy the prohibited alternatives. Biosphere maintenance supports continued habitation; it does not establish an individual guarantee of food, shelter or care, so guarantees remain unresolved. Useful farming, craft, government and other human activity stays visible, and preindustrial life provides no all-person nonworking census. The record describes the actual restrictive period, without promoting the original colony plan or a later negotiated solution into an unverified provision system.

guarantees.basis: Actual nanotechnological ecosystem support coexists with enforced destruction of advanced human technology and continuing preindustrial labor.

control.basis: Autonomous Winds determine the permitted technological ceiling despite local human aristocracies.

societies.name: Lockstep — Individually owned robot workforces
societies.society: The founding-family empire’s robot-supported waking economy

scope.continuity: Lockstep novel and author’s specific robot-economy explanation
scope.period: Established synchronized empire before Toby’s challenge changes its order
scope.population: Living humans during active waking cycles
exclusions: Hibernation calendar time as active leisure
The author’s real-world minimum-income preferences as fictional law
Political tyranny as proof that the family owns every robot

societies.description:
Lockstep civilizations sleep for long intervals while robots prepare food, repair environments and maintain settlements for the next waking cycle. The author explains a distinctive ownership rule: individuals hold general robot workforces and receive their earnings, whereas corporations may own only specialized machines. This is actual technological production supporting human consumption and income without equivalent personal labor.

Productive assets are meaningfully dispersed among individuals, giving control a favorable distributed-human estimate. That differs from political sovereignty: the founding family can weaponize hibernation access and impose severe exclusion. Guarantees are consequently uncertain and placed slightly toward the weak side, with a wide interval for ordinarily prosperous support versus coercive loss of the system. The record does not infer an unconditional basic-income law from the author’s separate real-world policy discussion. Nonworking remains null because decades asleep are not active leisure, and residents can still trade, govern, create, care and perform useful work when awake.

guarantees.basis: Robots supply food and maintain settlements, while individual owners receive robot-workforce profits; access can be coercively restricted through the cycle system.

control.basis: The author explicitly disperses general robot ownership among individuals, while the founding family’s political power remains a major qualification.

nonworking.basis: No awake-population census exists; long hibernation intervals must not be converted to a nonworking percentage.

societies.name: Polity — Earth before the Quiet War
societies.society: Machine industry and state-supported humans under corporate-political elites

scope.continuity: Neal Asher’s Polity setting encyclopedia, Earth Central historical entry
scope.period: Established Earth economy before the Quiet War and autonomous AI takeover
exclusions: Every colony as having the same benefits
State handouts as a verified comprehensive necessities charter

societies.description:
Before the Quiet War, most industry is already run by machines and much of the lower-class population depends on state handouts. The Earth Central computer administers budgets, taxes and services for the corporate-political class. This establishes an implemented automation-and-support economy rather than a future plan. Guarantees receive only a modest favorable estimate because support exists but its adequacy, coverage and enforceability are not established in the short author entry.

Effective authority remains with human politicians and corporate leaders, who direct the administrative machine and concentrate economic power. Control therefore sits near the human-elite position. The later AI takeover is a materially different period, not retroactively the sovereign of this earlier order. Benefit dependence also does not measure all useful activity: people can still provide care, culture, research or informal services. Nonworking remains unresolved. The point is narrowly historical Earth, without extending its precise institutions to every Polity colony or interpreting the entry’s polemical portrayal as a neutral welfare census.

control.basis: Corporate-political human elites direct the computer and concentrate decision-making before the Quiet War.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary research, care, creation, administration and maintenance remain work.

societies.name: Polity — AI-governed civilian economy
societies.society: Established civilian production under Earth Central and the Polity AIs

scope.continuity: Cormac-era Polity setting and author encyclopedia
scope.period: Established post-Quiet War Polity civilian life before a particular local emergency
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived civilian residents of functioning Polity worlds
exclusions: Every frontier/war zone as equally supplied
Economic security as free access to every premium good

societies.description:
After the Quiet War, Earth Central becomes the decisive ruler rather than a bureaucratic tool of human elites. Mature manufacturing and transport support the civilian economy, while the scholarly account characterizes residents as gaining economic security at the cost of self-government and privacy. Guarantees are provisionally favorable, with a broad interval because neither source supplies a complete universal benefits charter. Money and private transactions continue and are not mistaken for proof that basic support must be absent.

Ultimate authority lies with the Polity AIs, near the autonomous-machine end. Human firms, occupations and choices persist without establishing a right to overrule that hierarchy. This period is counted separately from prewar Earth because the source explicitly changes effective sovereignty over an already machine-centered productive order. Active human-derived residents are a disclosed proxy, while recordings and war casualties are excluded. Scientific, artistic, military and care work remains useful; economic security and strong AI rule do not provide an all-person nonworking rate, so participation stays null.
